A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MuseGNN. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite retitling, reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification accuracies, training timings, sampling and coupling-parameter ablations, and empirical convergence curves.

after.justification: v2 retains original MuseGNN experiments and adds comparisons and ablation results. Some baseline scores are explicitly taken from prior publications, but original empirical results are clearly present.

M1.justification: The sampling-based energy, proximal embedding updates, online mean estimator, training loss and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure. The expressivity analysis and expanded implementation explanations do not introduce a new MuseGNN component.

E1.justification: Empirical coverage remains homogeneous OGB/IGB node classification, including homogenized MAG240M. IGB-medium adds an intermediate graph-size setting within the already covered IGB family; the PDFs identify no new domain, population or prediction task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SGFormer, MariusGNN, FreshGNN, LazyGNN and USP while retaining the original comparators. Table 3 adds LazyGNN timing, and new Appendix Table 5 compares SGC, SIGN, Cluster-GCN and GraphFM. USP and the Table 5 baseline scores are explicitly literature-sourced.

E3.justification: Added comparisons introduce neighbor sampling for SGFormer on every dataset and specified METIS partition counts for LazyGNN. The coupling study also adds the 10-million-node IGB-medium setting. Existing MuseGNN architecture, sampling fanouts, optimization settings and timing hardware remain unchanged; the official-split statement is newly disclosed information.

E4.justification: The coupling-parameter sensitivity study expands from papers100M alone in v1 Table 4 to include arxiv, IGB-tiny, IGB-medium and products in v2 Table 6. This broadens an existing ablation question. The sampling comparisons and upper-level convergence experiment are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A explicitly discusses five LazyGNN trials and explains reporting mean accuracy with error bars rather than the maximum. Existing uncertainty-reporting practices otherwise persist, including omitted baseline error bars on the largest datasets. No increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises MuseGNN accuracy from 72.80 to 73.42 on IGB-tiny, 80.47 to 81.23 on products, 67.26 to 67.67 on MAG240M, and 60.21 to 61.74 on IGB-full. Numerous comparator and coupling-ablation results are added. The PDFs do not establish why the four retained benchmark scores changed, so these are revised reported outcomes rather than demonstrated gains under identical settings.

T1.justification: New Appendix C adds Proposition C.1 and its proof concerning WL-indistinguishable graphs and full-graph energy minimizers. It also develops normalized-Laplacian examples illustrating greater distinguishing power from sampled-subgraph energies. The original sampling-equivalence and convergence proofs remain in the renumbered Appendix E.

C1.justification: v2 adds a prominent contribution claim that sampling-based energies can be provably more expressive than the original full-graph energy. This expands the paper's central theoretical contribution beyond scalable, convergent energy minimization. The original scalability and competitive-accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 suggests greater expressivity as a possible explanation for effective small coupling values, proposes historical-embedding staleness as an explanation for LazyGNN's degradation, and discusses heterogeneous-graph extensions in Appendix F. It omits v1's specific prediction-attribution heuristics based on comparing embeddings, base predictions and shared means.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix A explicitly withholds code pending a publication decision; v2 announces source-code availability and supplies a repository link. v2 also documents official dataset splits, LazyGNN partition counts and author-provided configurations, and the provenance of borrowed baseline results. Core MuseGNN implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through discussion of USP, direct comparisons with LazyGNN, and connections to WL tests and subgraph-GNN expressivity. Sections 2.3 and Appendix B.5 distinguish MuseGNN's energy formulation and convergence guarantees from USP. Additional scalable-model literature further broadens the comparison context.

P1.justification: The title, author block, terminology and several motivation/comparison paragraphs are revised. Appendices gain dedicated expressivity, limitations and impact sections. The main section sequence and most method and convergence-proof exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a method-properties table, an additional-baseline table and a graph-expressivity illustration; expands several existing tables; and moves dataset statistics into Appendix A. Figure 1 is relocated and redrawn, while the original upper-level loss curve becomes Figure 3. The ICLR formatting and narrower Algorithm 1 substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence against other scalable UGNNs through LazyGNN and USP comparisons with documented settings. Broader coupling studies, the new expressivity analysis and reported code availability strengthen validation, explanation and reproducibility. Literature-sourced comparisons and unexplained revisions to some accuracies still limit interpretation, but the added support for the central scalability contribution establishes a substantial overall improvement.
